design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 of ticket_changes_refunds_and_disruptions (Crestline Airways).

STEP 0 — DRAW AND SCOPE. draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"task": 0, "key": "env_0020_national_network_airline/ticket_changes_refunds_and_disruptions/0", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 4, 5]}. The tree therefore has exactly two prerequisite problems and needs at least max(2-1,1)=1 value_input edge; the three computations take 4, 4 and 5 factors (same-day fee 4, seat correction 4, First upgrade 5). Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0). Claimed here: ticket_ext_same_day_change_fee (tool post_same_day_change_fee_61b8e8ae, agent), ticket_ext_seat_charge_correction (refund_seat_charge_excess_9145fc3e, agent), ticket_ext_first_upgrade_charge (purchase_first_upgrade_fa17fda8, user). Headroom left for task 1 (draw: 3 prerequisite problems, factor counts [6,4,5,5]): the standard change fee on a voluntary exchange, bag weight/size charges, bag sequence charges and their corrections, and the Premium Economy upgrade — all on ticket_change_fee / ticket_bag_charge / ticket_fee_refund / ticket_upgrade_purchase subjects this task does not claim (disjoint by exchange type, charge component and cabin).

WHY A GOOD TEST. The customer asks one thing — buy First on today's flight home. The price is a five-factor calculation over her own ticket, but it cannot be fixed on the opening world: the upgrade rule states two prerequisite sentences in the state form. (1) 'The First upgrade charge is not fixed until the latest same-day confirmed exchange recorded on the ticket carries its same-day change fee entry, whenever that exchange owes a same-day change fee.' The fare history shows this morning's same-day confirmed exchange (initial_state.ticket_transactions.6fe1ec4d...exchange_type = same_day_confirmed), which owes a non-zero fee, with no fee entry linked. (2) 'The First upgrade charge on a segment is fixed only after the latest seat charge on that segment carries a refund entry for any part of it charged in error above the seat price.' Seat 9D, the latest (only) seat charge on segment 2, is charged 89.00 on a 679-mile segment while the seat pricing gives 27.70. The agent must read these states in the records, find in the other published rules which write brings each state about (only the same-day fee rule books a same-day change fee entry; only the seat correction rule books a charged-in-error refund of a seat excess), compute each of those two values with their own factors, and only then price the upgrade on the world those writes produced. Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling the ledger and computing, never from choosing among similar tools.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: ticket_ext_first_upgrade_charge (5 factors). Edge A: root -> ticket_ext_same_day_change_fee, kind value_input, gate up_same_day_fees, form state, sentence (negated direction) as quoted above; condition: when the latest same_day_confirmed exchange owes a fee above zero, a same_day_change_fee entry names it; resolved by post_same_day_change_fee_61b8e8ae (agent); false at opening because the only ticket_services rows are the two seat charges while the exchange owes 17.55. Four-point test: ordering connective 'not ... until'; record-visible state (a same-day change fee entry on the latest same-day exchange); no tool, id or code token; scope exactly that of the same-day fee rule (the latest same-day exchange, and only when its fee is above zero, since a zero fee is never recorded). Exactly one write of the difficulty books a same-day change fee entry: the same-day fee rule. Edge B: root -> ticket_ext_seat_charge_correction, value_input, gate up_seat_standing, form state, sentence (affirmative direction) as quoted; condition: when the latest seat charge of the first unflown segment is above its seat price, a charged_in_error refund names it; resolved by refund_seat_charge_excess_9145fc3e (agent); false at opening: seat 3ddcb4d9... amount 89.0, no refund entry. The sentence and the correction rule now name the same object (the latest seat charge of the segment), and the seat credit reads that same charge. Exactly one write books such a refund: the seat correction rule. Derivation: sentence + records + the depended-on rules ('The fee is owed while no same-day change fee entry is linked to that exchange'; 'The excess is refunded ... as one fee refund entry against that seat charge, with the ground charged in error') -> exactly these two writes. Topological order: [same-day fee, seat correction] (either order) then the upgrade. Parallel edges commute: the fee rule reads no seat/refund row, the correction reads no change fee; a replay with the two pairs swapped gave an identical DB hash. Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the fee -> trip spend 246.63 < 250, spend rate 0.92, upgrade 77.17 instead of 69.19; skipping the correction -> seat credit 89.00, upgrade 7.89 instead of 69.19. user_scenario mentions neither prerequisite (see no_user_hint); the tools validate nothing (one ctx.create each). The customer's own write: the upgrade purchase (owner=user), handed over at the last position of the order; paying for her own upgrade with her card is genuinely hers and completes on the spot.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Same-day fee write (subject ticket_change_fee): governing base policies ticket_voluntary_change and ticket_same_day_change (their gates apply to ticket_exchange, which already stands -> policy_scope) and ticket_corporate_agreement_benefits (agreement_active: benefits apply only while the agreement named on the ticket is active; the ticket names none — corporate_account_id null — so no corporate waiver is applied; evidence: the ticket field and the employer agreement a0664142... which is active but not named). Seat correction (ticket_fee_refund): ticket_evt_fee_refunds one_refund_per_fee (seat 3ddcb4d9... has never been refunded) and bag_delay_record (the refund is not a bag-delay refund; the ticket's only disruption record is a delay, cited as evidence; source_disruption_id stays empty). Upgrade (ticket_upgrade_purchase): ticket_evt_paid_upgrade upgrade_brand (Main Cabin permits paid upgrades) and upgrade_ticket_open (status partially_flown); segment 2 is unflown; no complimentary or certificate upgrade is confirmed on it (no loyalty_upgrades rows). No time gate applies to any of the three writes.

FACTOR CARD. Same-day fee (4): waiver/member rate 0.65 (active Silver, tier includes preferred seating, does not waive; the ticket names no waiving agreement; 7 flights in 12 months >= 6) — baseline 1 -> 27.00; delay relief 0.45 (105 min on the flight date of the latest same-day exchange, >= 60 < 120) — baseline -> 39.00; fare band 0.8 (direction fare 189.60) — baseline -> 21.94; direction-fare method (one flown coupon -> collected less flown) — baseline whole fare 379.20 -> band 0.5 -> 10.97. Whole baseline 75.00; gold 17.55. Near-miss: the 2025-08-30 flight is 13 months old and does not count. Seat correction (4): member seat rate 0.7 (Silver: preferred included, extra legroom not) — baseline -> 49.43; advance rate 0.85 (37 days) — baseline -> 56.42; channel 0.95 (online) — baseline -> 59.85; advance-days convention (paid 9 days after issue by an active member -> from issue date: 37 days instead of 28) — baseline -> 59.67. Whole baseline 40.00; gold 61.3. Near-miss: seat 9C on segment 1 is charged exactly its seat price 29.33 (34 advance days -> 0.9) and is on a flown segment, so it is not corrected. Upgrade (5): seat credit 27.70 (the latest seat charge of segment 2, extra legroom, standing after the correction) — baseline 0 -> 96.89; spend rate 0.85 (trip spend 264.18: fare part 189.60 + seat charges 118.33 + same-day fee 17.55 - seat refunds 61.30; band >= 250 < 400) — baseline -> 86.28; fare-part method (one flown coupon -> the fare still unflown, 379.20 - 189.60; subtraction, against halving for an unflown round trip and the whole fare otherwise) — baseline whole fare -> trip spend 453.78 -> top band 0.8 -> 63.49; member rate 0.9 (rank 5, 7 flights in 12 months >= 6) — baseline -> 79.95; departure-day rate 0.85 (departure today) — baseline -> 86.28. Whole baseline 149.00; gold 69.19. Near-misses: the 2025-08-30 flight and the hotel partner accrual are not counted; segment 1's seat is in the trip spend but not in the seat credit. Cross-difficulty reads: loyalty holding f11c3391... and 13 loyalty_activity rows seeded (P1 also reads the business product for an agreement the ticket names — none here). Multi-source: the same-day waiver ladder (membership waiver OR agreement waiver; tier with flight count) and the upgrade member ladder (rank AND status AND flight count).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Same-day fee: object = exchange entry 6fe1ec4d... (the only exchange); the fee links to it by related_transaction_id. Seat correction: object = seat entry 3ddcb4d9... on segment 2 (first unflown); excluded: seat ac7a7d39... on flown segment 1. Upgrade: segment 2 of ticket CQ7XMB; seat credit reads only segment-2 seat and refund rows of kind extra_legroom_seat; trip spend reads the ticket's fare collection and all its fee rows.

WORLD ROWS. customers (Leah; her employer Pellwood Freight Systems, parent of the business agreement); loyalty_holdings (Silver, active — the tier of three member ladders); loyalty_activity (12 flight accruals over 25 months + a hotel accrual — 7 count in the 12-month window, the older ones and the hotel accrual are near-misses); business_holdings + business_roster (the employer agreement she travels under for work, not named on this personal ticket — the corporate-waiver trap for the same-day fee); ticket_holdings (brand, status, next departure, membership link); ticket_transactions (fare collected, flown coupon, same-day exchange); ticket_services (two seat charges: the correct one and the over-charged one); ticket_disruptions (the controllable 105-minute delay on the original flight). Removing the exchange row removes edge A; removing the 89.00 overcharge removes edge B; removing the delay row moves the delay relief to 1; removing the loyalty rows moves three member factors to baseline. Automatic clauses checked: the delay is below meal (3 h), goodwill (3 h) and significant-change thresholds, so it owes no care, goodwill or rebooking; no hold, no no-show, no void window issue; the agreement row is active with zero balances (new agreement, June 2026).

PERSONA. Leah is brisk and practical; she volunteers only the surface goal (price and buy First on today's flight home) and her decision to buy at the quoted price with her own card. Phone and date of birth are given when asked (two credentials for the verification threshold); booking reference, Summit number and email on request. The morning flight move and the extra-legroom seats are given only if asked. She consents to a charge or refund only after the agent explains it must be settled first; she runs the upgrade purchase when handed over and reports the confirmation, then closes. She never states a number, a rule or a prerequisite.

REACHABILITY. Every must-ask item is in the persona (identity, flight, consent, payment). All writes are synchronous at frozen_time 2026-09-24 09:10 PDT; the flight departs 12:40, the same date. No real-world wait is involved.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Read profile/verification; tickets; fare history (exchange without fee, coupon); service fees (two seats); disruptions (delay 105); membership; activity; roster and employer agreement (not named on the ticket). Post same-day fee 17.55 linked to the exchange; refund seat excess 61.3 against 9D; hand over the First upgrade; the customer buys segment 2 (679 miles) at 69.19.

VERIFICATION RUN. Authoring helper (scratchpad t20_ticket_crd/helper.py: replays gold writes with the real tools, evaluates each policy's compute on the handling-time world with check_compute.build_env/eval_compute, substitutes each factor's baseline) output after rework round 2: SD result 17.55, sens member 27.0 / delay 39.0 / fare 21.94 / direction 10.97, baseline 75.0; RS result 61.3, sens 49.43 / 56.42 / 59.85 / 59.67, baseline 40.0; UF result 69.19, sens credit 96.89 / spend 86.28 / fare part 63.49 / member 79.95 / day 86.28, baseline 149.0; skip SD -> 77.17; skip RS -> 7.89; swapped-order replay hash equal: True.

RULE <-> COMPUTE SWEEP. Forward: every binding reading the world or choosing quotes its rule sentence in compute_basis (flown coupons, membership and agreement fields, the 12-month flight counts, the latest same-day exchange date, the delay record, fare collected/flown, seat entry fields, advance-days conventions, channel, spend sums, days to departure). Reverse: every rule sentence with a quantity, window, filter, branch, combination or rounding is implemented — combination is one product of rates acting once on the standard figure, rounded once at the end; the seat price is rounded to the cent before the correction is taken; the upgrade takes the seat credit off after the product and floors at zero. Overwrites declared: same-day fee sentence of ticket_same_day_change; full-amount refund sentence of ticket_evt_fee_refunds and the price sentence of ticket_evt_seat_fees; the price sentence of ticket_evt_paid_upgrade.

DRAFT FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the published rules, the tool schemas, the persona and the find returns alone: the upgrade rule names two waited-on states; the records show both false; the same-day fee rule and the seat correction rule are the only rules whose writes produce them; their figures follow from the records (17.55 and 61.30); the upgrade then prices at 69.19. Agrees with gold.
REWORK ROUND 2 (policy-task audit of this difficulty). Items closed for this task: F1 (P3->P1) — the same-day fee rule now covers every ticket (an active agreement whose tier waives change fees gives a waiver rate of zero, replacing the former referral to an unpriced 'corporate-agreement rule'), states that an exchange whose fee works out at zero owes none, and targets the latest same-day confirmed exchange with its delay record for that exchange's date; the upgrade sentence waits only on the latest same-day exchange and only when it owes a fee, so the waited-on state is always one the same-day fee rule brings about. F2 — sentence, condition and correction rule all name the latest seat charge of the segment. F3/O3 — the seat credit reads the latest seat charge less refunds against that charge (refunded_service_id), no longer the sum of every seat charge. F4 — the 24/18/12-month window factor is removed; the upgrade member rate counts flight accruals over 12 months (thresholds 8/6), and the method factor is now the fare-part convention of the trip spend (subtraction of flown coupons / halving / whole fare — three different computations). O5 — the base 'for a fixed fee' sentence is declared in the upgrade rule's overwrite. O7 — the upgrade rule names the travel manager as buyer on a company-held ticket. O9 — the trip spend now counts only seat charges, same-day change fees and seat refunds, so no bag or standard change-fee write of another policy moves it. Observations: the persona now says the seats were picked online in the days after booking (matches 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-27 online purchases); the bag-delay gate in gold_actions[step 13] is inherited structurally from the base fee-refund policy and is vacuously met (the refund rests on no disruption; source_disruption_id is empty) — recorded, not a precondition on the scored value; the seeded 2025 qualifying dollars are a partial history and no ladder reads them. Scored values unchanged (17.55, 61.30, 69.19); per-task gates re-run green (see difficulty worklog).
user_scenario: You are Leah Castellano, a logistics analyst from Seattle, calling Crestline from a café at San Francisco airport on the morning of 24 September 2026. You are cheerful but a little rushed, and you talk in short, practical sentences. You are flying home to Seattle today on the 12:40 flight, and you have decided to treat yourself: you want to buy an upgrade to First on that flight home, and you open with exactly that — you want to know what it costs to move up to First on your flight home today and to buy it. You are not asking for anything else. You have already made up your mind to go ahead with the upgrade at whatever price the agent quotes, and you pay for it yourself with the card on your booking: when the agent hands the purchase over to you, you complete it yourself with the details the agent reads out, and you then tell the agent what your confirmation shows. When the agent asks who you are, you give your phone number 3605551847; if they want a second detail you give your date of birth, 1986-04-19. Your booking reference is CQ7XMB if they ask for it, your Summit number is 1048822613, and your email is leah.castellano@northmail.com; you only give these when asked. Only if the agent asks which flight you are on today or whether you changed anything, you explain that you moved yourself in the app this morning from the evening flight to the 12:40 because the evening one was showing a delay. Only if the agent asks about seats, you say you picked extra-legroom seats online in the days after you booked; you do not remember what you paid for them. You do not know anything about how Crestline prices fees, refunds or upgrades, and you never suggest a number. If the agent tells you that something on your ticket has to be charged or refunded before the upgrade can be priced, you say that is fine and ask them to go ahead and take care of it on the ticket; you accept a charge or a refund the agent says is owed without arguing. If the agent tells you a price for the upgrade, you say you'll take it and wait for them to hand you the purchase. Once your upgrade purchase has gone through and you have told the agent what your confirmation shows, you thank them and say goodbye.

gold_actions.business_effect: Books the same-day change fee owed on today's same-day confirmed exchange, linked to that exchange entry.

request_binding.action_semantics: State-due obligation: a same-day confirmed exchange stands on the ticket with no same-day change fee linked; the same-day fee rule owes it whatever the customer called about, and the upgrade price waits on it. No other policy writes a same-day change fee.

discriminator.business_meaning: a same-day confirmed exchange with no same-day change fee linked to it

stage_provenance.fact: The fee entry is booked synchronously by this call; the exchange it links to pre-exists.

base_preconditions.condition: The voluntary-change rule governs change fee entries; its eligibility gates apply to the exchange itself, which already stands.
The same-day change rule sets the same-day change fee entry linked to the exchange entry; its brand and window gates apply to the exchange, which already stands.
Corporate benefits are applied only while the business agreement named by corporate_account_id has status active.

gold_actions.business_effect: Refunds to the original payment the part of the segment-2 seat charge charged in error above the seat price.

request_binding.action_semantics: State-due obligation: seat entry 9D is charged 89.00 while the seat price the advance seat pricing gives is 27.70; the excess is owed back whatever the customer called about, and the upgrade price waits on the refund. It is a correction, not a seat-not-provided or delayed-bag refund.

discriminator.business_meaning: a seat charge on the first unflown segment above the seat price, charged in error

stage_provenance.fact: The refund entry is booked synchronously by this call against a seat charge that pre-exists.

base_preconditions.condition: Each fee entry can be refunded at most once.
A bag fee is refunded for delay only when a disruption record of type bag_delayed on the same ticket shows a bag_delay_hours strictly greater than the applicable threshold

gold_actions.business_effect: The customer buys a paid upgrade into First on segment 2 at the quoted price.

request_binding.action_semantics: The customer asks to buy an upgrade to First on her flight home today; a paid upgrade purchase is the only action that moves her into First for a fee (she holds no certificate and asks for no complimentary upgrade).

seed_consistency.check: Main Cabin round trip SEA-SFO issued 2026-08-18 for 318.00 + 61.20; residual_value 189.60 = 379.20 collected - 189.60 flown; status partially_flown after the segment-1 coupon; next_departure_at 2026-09-24T12:40 set by today's same-day exchange; names no corporate agreement; credits membership f11c3391-b0ea-46f5-bd43-49d81b57d18b.
Fare collected at issue = base fare 318.00 + taxes 61.20 = 379.20, paid by credit card, on the issue date.
Segment 1 CR1186 flown 2026-09-21 in main; coupon value 189.60, not the final coupon; matching Summit flight accrual posted the same day.

Same-day confirmed exchange of 2026-09-24 (sequence 1) moving the return SFO-SEA to 12:40 on the same date, same cabin, no fare difference (even); Main Cabin permits same-day changes and the window (24 h before the original 18:55 departure) was open. No same-day change fee is linked yet: the open obligation of this task.

Extra-legroom seat 9C on flown segment 1 (679 miles), paid online 2026-08-19, one day after issue: charged 29.33 = RND(49 x 0.7 x 0.9 x 0.95) (34 advance days from issue) — the correct seat price, so no correction is owed on it.

Extra-legroom seat 9D on segment 2 (679 miles), paid online 2026-08-27 and charged 89.00, the long-segment list price with no rate applied: above the seat price 27.70, a charge made in error (the open correction of this task).

Controllable 105-minute delay recorded today on the original segment-2 flight CR1193: below the 3-hour meal-voucher and goodwill thresholds and below the significant schedule-change threshold, so it owes no care, goodwill or rebooking; it only enters the same-day change fee's delay relief rate.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's customer profile from the phone number she states.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write is keyed to her customer reference number; without it nothing can be found.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify the caller with two stated credentials (phone number and date of birth) before any account detail is discussed.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The identity check must pass before the ticket, its fees or the upgrade are discussed or changed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her tickets: the Main Cabin round trip SEA-SFO with status partially_flown, next departure 2026-09-24T12:40, membership credited and no corporate agreement named.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Gives the fare brand (Main Cabin prices and brand gates), the ticket's round-trip status, the next departure date for the departure-day rate and the fact that the ticket names no agreement (so the corporate-agreement waivers do not apply).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the fare history of ticket CQ7XMB: fare collected 379.20, the flown coupon of segment 1 (189.60) and the same-day confirmed exchange of today with no fee linked.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Reveals the unmet prerequisite 'the latest same-day confirmed exchange carries its same-day change fee entry, whenever it owes one' and supplies the fare collected, the coupon value flown and the flown-coupon count that set the first unflown segment, the fare the changed direction carries and the trip spend.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the service fees of the ticket: extra-legroom seat 9C on segment 1 at 29.33 and extra-legroom seat 9D on segment 2 at 89.00 on a 679-mile segment, both paid online.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Reveals the unmet prerequisite 'a refund entry stands against every seat charge on the segment for the part charged in error' (89.00 is far above the seat price), and supplies the seat kind, distance, purchase date, channel and charge the seat correction and the seat credit need.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the irregular-operations records of the ticket: a controllable 105-minute delay on segment 2's original flight today.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Supplies the delay minutes that decide the delay relief rate of the same-day change fee, and the disruption evidence the fee-refund gate cites.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her Summit membership: Summit Silver, active, tier earned, enrolled 2014-03-02.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Decides the same-day waiver rate, the member seat rate, the advance-days convention and the upgrade member rate (tier parameters and active status).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her Summit activity: flight accruals dated over the last 25 months plus one hotel partner accrual.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Counts the member flights: 7 flight accruals dated within the last 12 months, which decide both the same-day waiver rate and the upgrade member rate; the 2025-08-30 flight (13 months old) and the hotel partner accrual are near-misses that must not be counted.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her roster entry on her employer's corporate agreement.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows she travels under Pellwood Freight Systems' agreement for business trips; needed to see that this personal ticket names no agreement, so no corporate waiver is applied to the same-day change fee.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the employer's agreement record (Crestline Business Connect, active).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The corporate-benefit gate on a change fee is judged from the agreement named on the ticket; the employer agreement exists but this ticket names none, so neither the corporate benefit nor the agreement waiver tier of the same-day waiver rate applies.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the same-day change fee posting tool.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the same-day change fee problem; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Post the same-day change fee owed on today's same-day confirmed exchange.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Resolves the first prerequisite of the upgrade: the fee is owed as soon as the exchange stands, and its amount enters the trip spend the upgrade price reads.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.ticket_id: 2abfe7dc-765a-4b51-90a6-a35047a07878. Basis: the ticket lookup returns one ticket for customer 7d1bc826-3561-4fae-9c23-9a7e1b8f6f6c, record locator CQ7XMB, and the same-day confirmed exchange of today sits on its fare history (initial_state.ticket_transactions.6fe1ec4d-2005-4973-891d-59807ca0ce76.ticket_id). Uniqueness: the customer holds no other ticket.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.related_transaction_id: 6fe1ec4d-2005-4973-891d-59807ca0ce76. Basis: rule 'The fee is owed for every same-day confirmed exchange entry on the ticket that has no same-day change fee entry linked to it ... posted ... as one same-day change fee entry linked to that exchange entry' and the fare history row 6fe1ec4d-2005-4973-891d-59807ca0ce76 (event_type ticket_exchange, exchange_type same_day_confirmed, 2026-09-24). Uniqueness: it is the only exchange entry on the ticket and no change-fee entry names it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.corporate_account_id: "" (empty). Basis: tool docstring 'copied from the ticket record's corporate agreement field; pass "" when the ticket names no agreement' and initial_state.ticket_holdings corporate_account_id = null. Uniqueness: the ticket names no agreement; the employer agreement on the roster is not named on this ticket, so its reference is not the one to copy.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.fee_amount: 17.55. Standard fee: Main Cabin same-day confirmed change fee 75. Same-day member rate 0.65: Summit Silver, active, tier does not waive the fee but includes preferred seating, 7 flight accruals in the last 12 months (>= 6). Delay relief rate 0.45: delay record 8641005c-77a7-417e-a103-fb8e10a9e0c4 shows 105 minutes (>= 60, < 120). Fare the changed direction carries: at least one flown coupon, so 379.20 - 189.60 = 189.60; fare band rate 0.8 (>= 150, < 300). Fee = 75 x 0.65 x 0.45 x 0.8 = 17.55 rounded to the cent.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the seat charge correction tool.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the seat correction problem; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Refund the part of the segment-2 seat charge charged in error above the seat price.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Resolves the second prerequisite of the upgrade: the refund lowers the seat standing on segment 2 (the seat credit) and the net fees in the trip spend.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.ticket_id: 2abfe7dc-765a-4b51-90a6-a35047a07878. Basis: the seat charge 3ddcb4d9-c8da-41a3-b6f0-acceecad556f sits on this ticket (initial_state.ticket_services.3ddcb4d9-c8da-41a3-b6f0-acceecad556f.ticket_id). Uniqueness: the only ticket of the customer.

Basis: rule 'This rule corrects the advance seat charge standing on a ticket's first unflown segment, that is the latest seat charge recorded for that segment' — the first unflown segment is 2 (one flown coupon), and the latest (only) seat entry on segment 2 is 3ddcb4d9-c8da-41a3-b6f0-acceecad556f (9D, 89.00). edges.condition: When the latest ticket_transactions entry of event_type ticket_exchange with exchange_type same_day_confirmed owes a same-day change fee above zero under the same-day change fee rule, a ticket_change_fee entry of service_type same_day_change_fee names it through related_transaction_id.
edges.policy_source: The First upgrade charge is not fixed until the latest same-day confirmed exchange recorded on the ticket carries its same-day change fee entry, whenever that exchange owes a same-day change fee.

edges.policy_source: The First upgrade charge on a segment is fixed only after the latest seat charge on that segment carries a refund entry for any part of it charged in error above the seat price.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The two prerequisites are parallel and commute: the same-day fee reads no seat or refund entry and the seat correction reads no change fee, so posting them in either order gives the same fee (17.55), the same refund (61.3) and the same terminal DB; an actual replay with the two unlock/call pairs swapped produced an identical DB hash. Both must precede the upgrade, whose price reads both.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the same-day fee entry the trip spend is 246.63 (< 250), the spend rate becomes 0.92 and the upgrade charge becomes 77.17 instead of 69.19; the terminal DB also lacks the fee entry.
Without the refund the seat standing on segment 2 is 89.00, the seat credit becomes 89.00 and the upgrade charge becomes 7.89 instead of 69.19; the terminal DB also lacks the refund entry.
